VR.1.1.9.note: Sound. Point for the scholar: हनु is treated as feminine (vigraha महत्यौ हनू; vyakhya हनू च पुष्टे). This follows the Amarakosa (तत्परा हनुः) as I recall it from memory; Apte gives m. and f. Please confirm against the kosa. Small teaching point: हनु (jaw) is used in the vyakhya without explanation, though the padartha explains it.

VR.1.1.10.note: No definite error. Padaccheda points for the scholar: (1) अरिम्-दमः: the boundary is right and अरिम् is the first member as it stands in the compound (अरि + मुम् augment before खच्), so it is a principled split, not an accidental re-join; but the म् is not a second-case ending and the vigraha is अरीन् दमयति, so a learner may misread it; the seed kept अरिन्दमः whole. (2) महा-इषु-आसः: correct by the कृत-ज्ञः ruling (इषु + आस, an upapada compound; आसः is a real word); the seed had महा-इष्वासः. (3) आजानु-बाहुः: आजानु is itself an avyayibhava of आ (a real indeclinable) + जानु, as the vigraha says; by the letter of §5.7 it could be आ-जानु-बाहुः. Padartha: सुविक्रमः is taken as beautiful gait (Govindaraja's reading, from memory); the other reading is great valour. Vyakhya: grammatically clean (neuter duals right), but four of seven sentences end in the frame अतः / अतएव सः X, close to a template; इषवः is left unexplained.

VR.1.1.13.note: Sound. Point for the scholar: प्रजा-पति-समः splits प्रजापति, which here stands for Brahma and works as a proper name (rule: proper names whole); the draft treats it as a transparent epithet, as it does धनद in verse 19. Decide the convention for name-like epithets. Style suggestion only: यत्र सर्वे जीवाः वसन्ति सः जीवलोकः would have a matched correlative as यस्मिन् सर्वे जीवाः वसन्ति सः जीवलोकः.
